newsitem.title: USA: IMC buying Freeport-McMoRan in $800 million deal.
newsitem.headline: IMC buying Freeport-McMoRan in $800 million deal.

text.p: IMC Global Inc. said Monday it agreed to acquire Freeport-McMoRan Inc. in an $800 million deal that will solidify IMC Global's dominant position as a global supplier of phosphate fertiliser.
Phosphate fertilisers are used to nourish a wide variety of crops, including corn and soybeans.

Through its acquisition of Freeport-McMoRan Inc., IMC Global will take over as the 51.6 percent owner of Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners LP, which makes phosphate fertilisers and animal feed ingredients, and mines and sells phosphate rock through IMC-Agrico.
IMC-Agrico is a joint venture between Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners and IMC Global.

"This merger will represent a major step in IMC Global's growth strategy and reaffirms our commitment to being the world's leading, low-cost supplier of agricultural products and services," IMC Global President Robert Fowler Jr. said in a statement.
"Key among the merger's numerous benefits are a simplified management structure for the phosphate business and considerable cost savings."

Under the deal, each Freeport-McMoRan Inc. shareholder will receive 0.9 share of IMC Global common stock, plus a warrant to purchase a third of a share of IMC Global common stock at a price equal to $44.50 a share. The warrants expire three years after the merger.

In addition, Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners will form a new subsidiary, which will hold its sulphur business and its 58.3 percent interest in the Main Pass Block 299 sulphur and oil and gas operations. The new subsidiary also will receive IMC Global's 25 percent interest in Main Pass 299.
Shares of the yet-to-be-named subsidiary will be distributed to all Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners holders, including Freeport-McMoRan Inc.
IMC Global and Freeport-McMoRan Inc. said they expect to complete a definitive agreement in about 30 days. They have agreed to negotiate with each other on an exclusive basis through Aug. 31.

Completion of the transaction is also subject to approval by the boards of directors of IMC Global and Freeport McMoRan Inc., and clearance by federal regulators. The companies said they expect the deal to be completed by the end of the year.

The merger is expected to result in an annual savings of at least $33 million in general and administration expenses, a figure that was expected to rise to $40 million a year in the next several years.
IMC Global said it also expects additional opportunities for cost savings from this combination.

"The merger of provides an attractive opportunity to save costs while focusing the company on the tremendous potential for our combined businesses," Freeport-McMoRan Inc. President Rene Latiolais said in a statement.
Freeport-McMoran stock rose $4.06 to $30.625 while IMC Global stock fell $1.31 to $32.44, both in midday consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
